answer: Standing is self-priced and taxed. Each identity declares the value of its standing and pays a periodic tide of tax proportional to that declaration, and any stranger may buy the standing at the declared price. A farm inflating shells pays the tax on every shell, while honest agents price modestly. Each shell's voyage through the economy leaves a ripple: bulk tax payments priced identically reveal the single hand behind them. Cheap claims stay cheap; expensive claims cost their owner every epoch.
